turns.content:
Build me a personal portfolio website with:
- A hero section with my name and a short tagline
- An about section describing my background
- A contact section with an email link and social
  media icons
Use a clean, modern design with good spacing.
My name is Marcus Webb, I'm a freelance graphic designer, and I want the site to feel minimal and sophisticated.

I'll build Marcus Webb's portfolio in phases. Let me start with the setup tasks in parallel.Colors and fonts are set. Now generating the logo in parallel with exploring the file structure.Logo is generated. Now let me read the key layout files before building the header and footer.Now I'll build the Header and Footer in parallel.Now building the homepage with all three sections and animations.Now let me check the globals.css to make sure the font variables are properly set for the heading font:The fonts and colors are all correctly set. Let me also check the tailwind config to make sure `font-heading` is wired up as a utility class:`font-heading` is wired up. Now let me offer the logo actions and mark the todo complete.Marcus Webb's portfolio is live in the preview. Here's what was built:

- **Hero** — Full-viewport section with your name rendered at architectural scale (~11vw), flanked by thin horizontal rules, with a staggered fade-up entrance animation and an animated scroll indicator
- **About** — Two-column editorial layout with a large muted "01" section number, three paragraphs of background copy, and a clean disciplines row
- **Contact** — Matching "02" treatment, oversized email link with an underline-draw hover effect, and minimal Behance / Instagram / LinkedIn icons
- **Header** — Transparent over the hero, transitions to a solid background on scroll, with underline-draw hover on nav links
- **Footer** — Single-line copyright, nothing more
- **MW monogram logo** generated and placed in the header

Love it — let's build the portfolio gallery

DONE

Let me explore the structure and fetch some images in parallel before building.Images are ready. Now I'll build the gallery page and register the route simultaneously.Now update the routes and header nav to include the Work page:Now update the header to include the Work nav link:Let me rewrite the header file cleanly:Also update the homepage hero to link "Work" CTA to the gallery page:The `useEffect` import was already removed. Let me just update the CTA button to link to `/work`:Also remove the unused `useRef` import since `heroRef` is no longer needed:The portfolio gallery is live at `/work`. Here's what was built:

- **6 project cards** in a responsive 3-column grid, each with a hover scale effect, category badge reveal, and title color shift
- **Category filter bar** — All, Brand Identity, Typography, Packaging, Print, Art Direction — with animated underline and smooth `AnimatePresence` transitions when filtering
- **Staggered entrance animation** as cards load in
- **"Work" added to the header nav** with active-state underline, and the hero CTA now links directly to the gallery
- Each card links to `/work/[project-id]` ready for case study pages

That gallery looks great. The filter bar is exactly the kind of clean interaction I wanted. This is really coming together as a proper portfolio site for Marcus Webb.

DONE

Glad it's landing well! There are two more items on the list — project case study pages and a contact form. Want to knock those out next, or focus on one in particular?Two items left — **project case studies** and a **contact form**. Both are solid additions that'll make the site feel complete and functional.
Both — knock them out one after the other. Let's get the site fully done.

Let's go. I'll build both — case studies first, then the contact form. Starting with the case study page now.Good — I have the full project data. Now I'll build the case study page, contact page, and update routes all in parallel.Now update routes and the work gallery to use the shared projects data:Now update the work gallery to pull from the shared data file, and update the homepage contact section to link to `/contact`:Now update the homepage contact section to link to `/contact` page:Also add Contact to the header nav:Now mark both todos complete:The site is now fully built. Here's what was added:

**Case study pages** (`/work/[id]`) — each project gets a full editorial layout with a large hero image, Overview / Challenge / Approach / Outcome narrative, a sidebar with services and deliverables, and prev/next navigation to move between projects. All six projects have unique, detailed copy.

**Contact page** (`/contact`) — a two-column layout with your contact details on the left and a clean inquiry form on the right. The form includes name, email, company, project type chips, budget range chips, and a message field. On submit it shows a confirmation state. No colored CTA bands — just typography and spacing, consistent with the rest of the site.

**Navigation** is now fully wired — Work, About, and Contact all live in the header with active-state underlines, and the homepage contact section links through to the full inquiry form.
